item.title: mlx-audio library brings TTS and STS models to Apple Silicon
item.description:
mlx-audio library brings TTS and STS models to Apple Silicon

Neywa Labs, the company behind Nativ, has released mlx-audio, an open-source library built on Apple’s MLX framework. The tool allows developers to run audio models directly on Apple Silicon (M series chips), supporting text-to-speech (TTS), speech-to-text (STT), speech-to-speech (STS), and music generation tasks with fast, optimized inference.

🧩 Core Capabilities

The library provides a suite of audio processing features:

  • Model Support: Multiple architectures for TTS, STT, STS, and music generation.
  • Multilingual Support: Language options vary by model, including English, Japanese, Chinese, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, and Hindi.
  • Voice Customization: Features for voice cloning and customization.
  • Control: Adjustable speech speed control.
  • Interface: An interactive web interface with 3D audio visualization.
  • API: An OpenAI-compatible REST API.
  • Quantization: Support for 3-bit, 4-bit, 6-bit, 8-bit, and more for optimized performance.

⚙️ Model Variants

The evidence lists specific model options available within the ecosystem:

Model Name Description
Kokoro Fast, high-quality multilingual TTS (EN, JA, ZH, FR, ES, IT, PT, HI) available in bf16, 8bit, 6bit, and 4bit.
KittenTTS Compact models for edge-friendly TTS (EN) in nano, micro, mini, and collection sizes.
Qwen3-TTS Custom voice model, e.g., “mlx-community/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B-CustomVoice-8bit”.

🚀 Installation and Usage

developers can install and interact with the library using the following methods:

  • Installation:
    • pip install -U mlx-audio
    • uv tool install --force mlx-audio --prerelease=allow
    • For development: git clone https://github.com/Blaizzy/mlx-audio.git followed by pip install -e ".[dev, server]"
  • Integration: Available as a Swift package for iOS and macOS integration.
  • CLI Generation:
    • Basic command: mlx_audio.tts.generate --model mlx-community/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B-CustomVoice-8bit --text 'Hello, world!' --voice Vivian
    • File handling: By default, generation saves numbered files such as audio_000.wav and audio_001.wav. Use --join_audio to save one combined file.
    • Streaming: When using --stream, add --save to write the streamed audio to disk.

#AppleSilicon #MLX #TextToSpeech #OpenSource #NeywaLabs #AudioAI

item.title: SDGym Benchmarking Framework Released for Synthetic Data Evaluation
item.description:
SDGym Benchmarking Framework Released for Synthetic Data Evaluation

The Synthetic Data Vault Project from DataCebo has introduced SDGym (Synthetic Data Gym), a benchmarking framework designed to model and generate synthetic data. This tool allows developers to measure performance, memory usage, and data quality across various modeling techniques, including classical statistics and deep learning.

🔍 Overview

SDGym integrates with the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) ecosystem, providing a way to evaluate synthesizers, datasets, and metrics. The project traces its origins to MIT’s Data to AI Lab in 2016, with DataCebo founded in 2020 to grow the ecosystem, which is now described as the largest for synthetic data generation and evaluation.

🧩 How it works

The framework allows users to benchmark techniques by selecting synthesizers and baselines, then running evaluations on publicly available or custom datasets. Key workflow steps include:

  • Defining which modeling techniques to use, such as GaussianCopulaSynthesizer and CTGANSynthesizer.
  • Selecting baselines, such as UniformSynthesizer.
  • Executing the benchmark using the function sdgym.benchmark_single_table.
  • Generating a detailed evaluation of performance, memory, and quality across the selected datasets.

Users can also customize the process by writing their own machine learning models, specifying training and sampling logic to test personal synthetic data generation techniques.

⚙️ Key details

  • Metrics: Measures performance, memory usage, synthetic data quality, and privacy.
  • Data Sources: Supports publicly available datasets from the SDV project and custom private datasets stored locally or on Amazon S3.
  • Customization: Allows users to include their own synthesizers, datasets, or metrics.
  • Installation: Available via pip or conda, with a recommendation to use a virtual environment to avoid software conflicts.

🚀 Availability

SDGym is part of the SDV library ecosystem. Developers can access the documentation and install the package to begin benchmarking immediately. The library includes a feature to list available datasets, facilitating quick setup for users wishing to test against standard public data.
